predecessors.name: Seljuk dynasty (before the empire)
predecessors.text: the Seljuk dynasty's Khorasan, held since 1037

predecessors.name: Ghaznavid Empire
predecessors.text: Khorasan, Herat, Sistan and Ghur lost by the Ghaznavids at Dandanaqan, 23 May 1040

successors.name: Khwarezmid dynasty (Anushtegin dynasty)
successors.text: Rayy, Hamadan and Isfahan: Tughril III was defeated and killed at the Battle of Rayy on 4 March 1194, and the Khwarazmians held Persian Iraq, including Isfahan, by 25 June 1194

successors.name: Eldiguzids
successors.text: the Atabegs of Azerbaijan, who became effectively independent after Sanjar's death in 1157 (Seljuk Empire page lists them among the successor states)

rulers.name: Mahmud II
rulers.title: Sultan of the western realm (Iraq and western Persia)

ledger.x: 1040: the Seljuks win Khorasan at Dandanaqan.
1040: Herat, Sistan and Ghur pass to the Seljuks.
1041: Kerman passes to the Kerman Seljuk line.
1041: Gorgan comes under Seljuk control.
1041: the Ziyarid ruler of Tabaristan pays tribute.
1043: Tughril takes Rayy.
1043: the seat moves from Nishapur to Rayy.
1043: the Seljuks drive Shah Malik out of Khwarezm.
1046: Ibrahim Inal takes Hamadan.
1047: Tughril besieges Isfahan.
1051: the seat moves to Isfahan.
1052: Isfahan surrenders.
1052: Tughril enters Isfahan and makes it his capital.
1054: Tughril takes Azerbaijan.
1054: the Shaddadid emir of Ganja submits.
1055: Tughril enters Baghdad and ends Buyid rule there.
1057: Mosul and Sinjar fall to the Seljuks.
1062: Fars passes to the Seljuks.
1062: Khuzestan is bridged in with Fars.
1064: Alp Arslan conquers Armenia, taking Ani.
1065: Alp Arslan subjugates Tbilisi.
ledger.cp: Tbilisi (emirate; not named further on the page)

ledger.x: 1068: Alp Arslan invades the Byzantine Empire.
1071: Alp Arslan wins at Manzikert.
1072: the Seljuks sell Ani to Manuchihr.
1073: Malik-Shah takes Termez.
1073: Atsiz takes Jerusalem.
1074: Kerman is reduced to vassalage.
1075: the Shaddadid vassalage of Ganja ends in annexation.
1075: Ganja and Dvin are annexed.
1076: Atsiz takes Damascus (see 1073).
1079: Georgia is made to submit.
1085: Fadl III revolts and takes Ganja.
1086: Malik-Shah conquers northern Syria.
1086: Malik-Shah retakes Ganja.
1087: Bukhara and Samarkand come under Seljuk rule.
1087: Malik-Shah's Transoxiana expedition reaches the Eastern Kara-Khanids.
1089: the expedition ends with the Eastern khan a vassal.
1089: the Eastern Kara-Khanid khan becomes a Seljuk vassal.
1090: the Nizari Ismailis end Ziyarid rule in Tabaristan.
1092: a bridging year.
1092: Malik-Shah dies and the empire splits.
ledger.cp: Seljuk Syria (Tutush I; Damascus and Aleppo lines)

ledger.x: 1118: Sanjar becomes sultan and the empire has two seats.
1121: the Seljuks are routed at Didgori on 12 August.
1127: Zengi is made governor of Mosul.
1135: Sanjar's army enters Ghaznavid land and reinstates Bahram Shah.
1138: Sanjar marches on Khwarezm.
1139: Mosul and the Jazira leave the Seljuk shape.
1141: Atsiz occupies Merv, Nishapur and Sarakhs.
1141: Sanjar loses Transoxiana at Qatwan.
1141: the Kara-Khanids pass from the Seljuks to the Qara Khitai.
1142: Sanjar expels Atsiz from Khorasan.
1143: Sanjar subdues Khwarezm again.
1143: Atsiz is made a vassal again.
1152: the Ghurids take Herat.
1152: Khwarezm leaves the Seljuk shape.
1152: Sanjar defeats the Ghurids at Nab, 24 June.
1153: Balkh falls to the Oghuz.
1153: the Oghuz defeat Sanjar and take him prisoner.
1157: Sanjar dies at Merv, 8 May.
1157: Khorasan passes out of Seljuk hands.
ledger.cp: Turkic and Turkmen rulers of Khorasan (Oghuz, Ay-Aba at Nishapur)

ledger.x: 1157: the Ghaznavid vassalage ends with Sanjar.
1160: the caliph's state replaces the Seljuk sultans' Iraq.
1187: the Kerman Seljuk line ends.
1193: Tekish takes Ray.
1194: Tughril III is killed at the Battle of Rayy, 4 March.
1194: the struggle for Rayy ends with the Seljuk defeat of 4 March.
1194: the Great Seljuk state ends at the Battle of Rayy.

wars.name: Battle of Dandanaqan
wars.outcome: Decisive Seljuk victory on 23 May 1040 near Merv; Khorasan, Herat, Sistan and Ghur pass to the Seljuks.

wars.name: Tughril's conquests in Iraq and Persia
wars.outcome: Gorgan and Tabaristan (1041-1042), Rayy (1042-1043), Isfahan (1052), Azerbaijan (1054), Baghdad (1055) and Mosul (1057) fall; Tughril receives the title 'King of the East and the West' in 1058.

wars.name: Battle of Manzikert
wars.outcome: Seljuk victory on 26 August 1071; Romanos IV taken prisoner for a week; Turkish settlement of Anatolia follows, outside the sultan's own border.

wars.name: Seljuk-Georgian wars
wars.outcome: Alp Arslan subjugates Tbilisi (1065); Seljuk amirs are beaten by George II (1073); Malik-Shah's second campaign (1078-1079) and George II's 1088 submission at Isfahan; the Seljuks are routed at Didgori on 12 August 1121.

wars.name: Qavurd's revolt and the Battle of Kerj Abu Dulaf
wars.outcome: Malik-Shah wins the three-day battle near Hamadan in 1073 and has Qavurd strangled; in 1074 he besieges Bardsir and stops when Sultan-Shah 'begged for forgiveness'.

wars.name: Malik-Shah's Syrian campaign
wars.outcome: Aleppo, Antioch, Edessa, Harran and Qal'at Ja'bar captured; the emirs of Anatolia fail at Nicaea c.

wars.name: Malik-Shah's Transoxiana expedition
wars.outcome: Malik-Shah takes Kara-Khanid castles (Bukhara, Samarkand, Balasagun, Isfijab, Kashgar); the Eastern khan Hasan ibn Suleiman becomes his vassal and the Turkistan Region 'up to the borders of China' is under Seljuk rule in 1089.

wars.name: Seljuk war of succession (Berkyaruq against Tutush)
wars.outcome: Tutush I was killed in battle against Berkyaruq in February 1096; Sanjar was made governor of Khorasan in 1097.

wars.name: First Crusade
wars.outcome: The Seljuk Empire infobox dates the First Crusade 1095-1099; no page opened gives a Great Seljuk action in it (the Levant is the Syrian Seljuk lines' ground in the correction).

wars.name: Sanjar's Khwarezm campaigns
wars.outcome: Hazarasp (1138), Atsiz's raid on Khorasan (1141-1142), Sanjar's march of 1143 and again of 1147 keep Khwarezm a vassal.

wars.name: Battle of Qatwan
wars.outcome: Decisive Qara Khitai victory on 9 September 1141; the Seljuks lose Transoxiana and Khwarezm turns to the Qara Khitai.

wars.name: Ghurid-Seljuk clash at Nab
wars.outcome: Sanjar defeats and captures Ala al-Din Husayn at Nab on 24 June 1152.

wars.name: Oghuz revolt and the capture of Sanjar
wars.outcome: Sanjar is defeated in April 1153, held until 1156, escapes and dies at Merv in 1157; Khorasan is left to Turkic and Turkmen rulers.

wars.name: Khwarezmid conquest of Persian Iraq (Battle of Rayy)
wars.outcome: Tekish takes Ray in January 1193, defeats and kills Tughril III on 4 March 1194 and holds Persian Iraq by 25 June 1194.

certainty.note: No frontier of the Great Seljuk state is fixed by treaty on any page opened: the steppe and desert edges, the Byzantine, Georgian and Crusader frontiers and the vassal tints are all approximate.
